pr_body:
Provides information about the security products registered on a Windows
system.

```
osquery> select * from windows_security_products;
                 type = Firewall
                 name = Windows Firewall
                state = Off
      state_timestamp = NULL
     remediation_path = %windir%\system32\firewall.cpl
signatures_up_to_date = 1

                 type = Antivirus
                 name = Windows Defender Antivirus
                state = On
      state_timestamp = Thu, 28 Feb 2019 00:37:22 GMT
     remediation_path = windowsdefender://
signatures_up_to_date = 0

                 type = Antispyware
                 name = Windows Defender Antivirus
                state = On
      state_timestamp = NULL
     remediation_path = windowsdefender://
signatures_up_to_date = 1
```

Thanks to @redplait for the initial prototype and @defensivedepth for
sponsoring completion of development.

Closes #4331
pr_comments: AFAICT the CI failure is unrelated. Please let me know what changes need to be made to merge this.
@akindyakov All of the C-style code comes directly from the Microsoft example code. I can convert to C++ style as requested.
All comments have been addressed and the integration test has been added. We can't do much on the integration test as we don't know which security products will be installed on a given system.

Okay, I found a path forward on the CI failures for this one. We now use a strategy in which the `wscapi.dll` is runtime linked rather than load-time linked. This allows the table to error and return no results rather than crashing the whole process if the dll is not available.
I believe this is ready to merge now, unless there are further comments. Thanks for the review y'all!

issue_context.title: Add vtable for Security Center (Windows)
issue_context.body:
Third-party security products are required to register themselves within the Windows Security Center (WSC). WSC interfaces directly with the security product to track changes in installation, configuration, and health, and with the Action Center, which notifies users of required actions (e.g. restart the firewall). 

This would be a fantastic vtable to add, as it would allow systems owners to introspect the WSC and identify all installed and registered security products on the system. This has the added advantage of not requiring inspection of installed application lists, and only showing software which has successfully registered with WSC. 

Example of querying WSC providers using WMI: 
```
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/SecurityCenter2 -ClassName AntiVirusProduct
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/SecurityCenter2 -ClassName AntiSpywareProduct 
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/SecurityCenter2 -ClassName FirewallProduct
```

There are three main enumerations which would be useful to add: 

WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER 
https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/bb432509(v=vs.85).aspx

WSC_SECURITY_PRODUCT_STATE 
https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/jj155490(v=vs.85).aspx

WSC_SECURITY_PROVIDER_HEALTH 
https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/bb432510(v=vs.85).aspx

Some example scenarios that could be solved with this vtable: 

- Tell me if there are systems without a WSC-registered security product.
- Tell me which systems have a WSC-registered security product disabled or in poor health.
- Tell me if a user has installed more than one security products.
- Tell me if a user has installed more than one firewalls. 

Some example rows and columns output: 

- Product Name | TEXT | Security Product Name
- Registration Type | TEXT | WSC Registration (e.g. Firewall, AntiVirus, AntiSpyware) 
- Binary Path | TEXT | Path to Binary

review_comments: I though you do release in scope guard, don't you?
Yes, in the case of error we have the scope guard to prevent leaking this. If we did not release it here, we would leak every product until the last one.
You called free on `PtrVal`, do you need to here?
No, because `ProductState` is allocated on the stack in this function.
You called free on PtrVal, do you need to here?
No, because `SignatureStatus` is allocated on the stack in this function.
No, because some systems (such as CI) will not return any data due to the `wscapi.dll` library failing to load, or because they have no registered security products.
